about.title: Lodi Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a car part gives out on Kettleman Lane, a machine malfunctions at a Lodi warehouse, or a household item causes burns in a kitchen off Lower Sacramento Road. San Joaquin County residents deal with these injuries alongside everyday recovery, often unsure who is responsible: the manufacturer, the distributor, or the store that sold it. Under California's strict liability framework, injured people frequently don't have to prove anyone was negligent, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That said, these cases hinge on evidence, and the product itself is often the most important piece. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent claimants directly. Instead, we connect Lodi residents free of charge with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, identify who may be liable, and explain next steps clearly, without pressure or upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Lodi Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Fight
items.desc: California often doesn't require proof of negligence in product cases — showing a defect caused the injury may be enough, which can change how a claim is approached from day one.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, and an attorney can help sort out which parties belong in the claim.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Because the product itself is often central to proving a defect, connecting with an attorney quickly can help make sure it's kept safe and properly documented.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability rules often focus on whether the product itself was defective and caused harm, rather than requiring proof of carelessness. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this may apply to your case.

items.question: What if the product was thrown away or damaged after my injury?
items.answer: It's still worth speaking with an attorney, since other evidence like photos, receipts, or medical records may help. That said, preserving the actual product whenever possible is one of the most useful things an injured person can do.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened in Lodi specifically?
items.answer: Local details can matter, such as where the product was purchased or used, but California product liability law applies statewide. An attorney familiar with San Joaquin County processes can walk you through what to expect locally.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
